cells.tense: Present — here, with the pen in your hand.
cells.verb: keeping going on your own reserves when things are tight
cells.place: in the place where you decide what you're aiming at
cells.ask: Let what you've been quietly carrying start carrying something you actually want, not just something you can survive — pick one hope and keep walking toward it where someone can see. What comes back is the kind of light that only shows up when something you tended has finished growing.
cells.core: You can hold a direction when nothing around you makes it easy. Not with a show of it — in private, out of what you've got, with no one checking. You say 'this' and you keep saying it, and the pressure isn't arguing you out of it. That's the kind of strength that doesn't need an audience, which is exactly why it's trustworthy.
cells.sheetLine: You hold your direction on your own reserves, and it holds.

cells.tense: Future — braced for a hardship that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: gritting through on your own reserves
cells.place: in the place where you decide what you're aiming at
cells.ask: Let one thing come in from someone else — take the help that's already been offered, or ask for one thing you'd normally carry alone, and let it be a fair trade rather than a debt. What comes back is a grip that holds without crushing what it's holding.
cells.core: You've decided you'll hold no matter what, and 'no matter what' has quietly become the whole plan. Somewhere ahead is a version of this where it gets much harder, and you're already living there — spending what you have in reserve on a weight that hasn't landed yet, and turning down hands because taking one would feel like giving ground. The direction is still yours. The clenching isn't helping it.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing to carry alone what nobody's handed you yet.

cells.tense: Past — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.place: in the place where you decide what you're aiming at
cells.ask: Rather than forcing yourself back to it, tell one person what you were aiming at and what it cost you to stop — plainly, so it's seen. Setting a thing down in the open stops being a defeat and starts being a finish, and what comes back is the capacity to hold something again without crushing yourself to do it.
cells.core: You picked a direction, it got hard in a practical, unglamorous way, and somewhere back there you let go of it. Nothing dramatic — the holding just stopped. And you're still standing where it stopped, half-facing the thing you put down. The strength to persist didn't disappear. It's just not pointed at anything right now, and that leaves the choosing with nowhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: You let go of the direction when it got hard, and you're still standing there.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: carrying through on your own reserves
cells.place: in the place where you decide what you're aiming at
cells.ask: Say what you're carrying this for — the one thing, in plain words, to yourself or to someone else. When the reason is named, the enduring turns out to have been aiming at something all along, and what comes back is a strength that holds its shape instead of just grinding.
cells.core: You're already holding a line through real pressure, every day, on your own reserves — and you'd call it having no choice. But the shape of what you keep carrying is a choice; you're saying 'this, not that' with your hands while your mouth says 'it's just how things are.' The steadiness is running. The one steering it hasn't admitted to being at the wheel.
cells.sheetLine: You're already choosing what you carry. You call it having no choice.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
